judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-4 Content statements (rank 3, identical canonical coordinate 'Class-4') under the same Competency C-2.3 and Curricular Goal CG-2. First: 'Skip counting and construction of multiplication tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9' (LCs: skip count by 6-9; construct tables of 6-9). Second: 'Understanding multiplication by 10' (LC tagged multiplication, place value, ten). They are coherent, mutually reinforcing facets of Class-4 multiplication: table construction by skip counting builds fact fluency, while multiplying by 10 rests on a place-value pattern rather than on the 6-9 tables specifically. The evidence shows topical coherence (shared token 'multiplication', same competency, adjacent source pages) but no substantive same-rank developmental dependency in either direction, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 33 omitted items), so absence of stronger sequencing language in the excerpts is not proof of absence in the full source.

judgment.rationale: First SFI is the Class-5 Content bullet 'Turns' under Competency C-3.3 (symmetry, reflection and rotation in familiar 2D/3D shapes), with LCs 'Recognize/Create turns (rotation) in familiar two- and three-dimensional shapes'. Second is the Class-3 Content bullet 'Models objects using these shapes' under C-3.1 (identifying, comparing and analysing attributes of 2D/3D shapes), with LC 'Model objects using 2D and 3D shapes'. Both sit under Curricular Goal CG-3 and involve hands-on work with familiar 2D and 3D shapes, so there is genuine same-domain spatial-geometry coherence and mutual reinforcement (modelling with shapes involves orienting and manipulating them; turns operate on such familiar shapes). However, the evidence does not show that shape-modelling proficiency substantively supports recognising or creating rotational turns: the two belong to different competency strands (attribute description vs. symmetry/rotation), and the only textual overlap is the generic token 'shapes' plus shared CG-3 ancestry, which is insufficient for a developmental Class-3 to Class-5 dependency. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and both carry upstream merge/audit context, and the shared ancestors lack developmental coordinates, so ancestry contributes no rank evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class-3 (rank 2) Content bullets under Competency C-3.2 ('Describes location and movement using common and mathematical language; understands the concept of a map'). The second SFI is 'Using directions to orient and move' (LCs: use directions to orient oneself; use directions to move from one place to another), i.e., direct use of directional language for orientation and movement. Command of directional orientation and movement substantively supports describing position and location within a route map, so at equal class rank the developmental support runs second-to-first; the pair-specific change is from direct bodily orientation/movement to representing and describing location on a map, not mere repetition. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-1 Content statements (rank 0, identical coordinate) under the same Competency C-1.7 ('Represents numbers up to 20 using the place-value system, reads number and number names, recognizes patterns in numbers'). First: 'Patterns in numbers up to 20' (LC: recognize patterns in numbers up to 20); second: 'Reads and writes the numbers up to 50' (LCs: read / write numbers up to 50). These are substantively coherent but distinct facets of early number sense — pattern recognition in the number sequence versus reading and writing numerals — that mutually reinforce work on the number sequence within the same competency. At equal developmental rank the evidence does not substantiate a directional dependency: neither the larger range (50 vs 20) nor the differing skill verbs shows that proficiency in one is what supports success in the other, and either direction could be argued equally, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards.
